verdict.rationale: Google Cloud's IAM lets admins define fine-grained roles and permissions, and Workload Identity Federation lets external workloads (including agent-like processes) access GCP resources via federated, short-lived credentials instead of long-lived service account keys — both directly support scoped, least-privilege credential issuance. However, none of the evidence specifically addresses issuing credentials scoped to an 'agent' persona (e.g., agent-specific API key restrictions, IAM Conditions, or short-lived OAuth token flows for AI agents), and there's no independent corroboration of this being used in agentic workflows. Missing for 10: agent-specific scoped-credential workflow docs, IAM Conditions/short-lived token examples, and independent/hands-on validation.
